spec.title: PROP-017: Public format coverage and compatibility inventory

status.comment: catalog and development gate; no consumer format migration

p.PUBLIC-FORMAT-CATALOG: The machine-readable compatibility inventory is `public-formats.json` beside this contract. Each row identifies a format, its owner, trust boundary, current schema version, compatibility, migration or refusal rule, fingerprint participation, governing contract and conformance test paths. The underlying contract and reader govern behavior; the catalog records that behavior and does not authorize a format migration.

p.PUBLIC-FORMAT-GAPS: A seam without an independent numeric version carries `version: null` and an explicit `versionGap` explaining the inherited version or the outstanding compatibility work. A missing version is never silently assigned version 1. A test path records existing coverage, not a claim that every requirement has a conformance test; `testGap` records known incomplete evidence.

p.PUBLIC-FORMAT-GATE: `npm run formats:check` lists formats and refuses a missing compatibility/migration policy, source/test evidence, duplicate identity or observed schema-version drift. Discovery scans TypeScript and JavaScript declarations, literal validators and object writers with `codkit`-prefixed property names in all package source directories and production tools, without executing them. Non-JSON seams, nested schema fields and manual validators are explicitly registered; named numeric version constants are checked against source.

p.PUBLIC-FORMAT-GATE-LIMIT: Discovery is a coverage tripwire for the established property and constant conventions, not an arbitrary program analyzer. A new format using computed keys, aliased validators, another version-field convention or dynamic version expressions requires an explicit catalog entry and discovery extension with a failing fixture. A compatibility checker does not replace runtime parser conformance tests.

p.PUBLIC-FORMAT-FREEZE: Changing a catalog row's version or migration policy requires reading its governing contract and reviewing the reader/writer change together. Catalog maintenance does not change serialized patchsets, delta fingerprints, generated history, executable type trust or licence policy.
